paragraphs: Friend, look at what Jacob does before he takes one step toward Egypt. He stops at Beersheba and offers sacrifices to God (Gen 46:1). Then God speaks to him: "Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there." (Gen 46:3) Big move, new country, and the first thing Jacob does is bring it to God.

Now hear the promise, because it's the heart of the whole passage. God says, "I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back." (Gen 46:4) Jacob doesn't have to know how the road ends, because God is going with him. I know a little about being carried somewhere you didn't pick, and I'm telling you, the best part of the trip is who's holding you.

And watch what Jacob does when he stands before the king of Egypt. He tells Pharaoh his years have been "few and hard" (Gen 47:9), and he still blesses Pharaoh coming in and going out (Gen 47:7, 10). Hard years didn't empty the man out. So here's the lesson for you, baker: when the road ahead is scary, hear God say "Do not be afraid," and let hard years be a reason to hold on to Him, not let go. And keep that apron on, because this family's story is a long way from finished.
